title: Structure-sheaf sections on an intersection are a filtered colimit
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $E\subset |X|$ be an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens. After replacing the family by its finite-intersection refinement, write $E=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ with each $U_i$ quasi-compact open and with $I$ directed by reverse inclusion: for every $i,j$ there is $k$ with $U_k\subseteq U_i\cap U_j$. Give $E$ the subspace topology and the inverse-image structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X|_E$ along the inclusion [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], and let $\rho_i:\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X|_{U_i})\to\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_X|_E)$ be the canonical restriction maps (the unit of the inverse image along $E\hookrightarrow U_i$). Then: (a) every $s\in\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_X|_E)$ equals $\rho_i(a)$ for some $i\in I$ and some $a\in\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X|_{U_i})$; (b) if $a,a'\in\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X|_{U_i})$ satisfy $\rho_i(a)=\rho_i(a')$, then $a|_{U_k}=a'|_{U_k}$ for some $k\in I$ with $U_k\subseteq U_i$. Equivalently, the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{i\in I}\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X|_{U_i})\longrightarrow\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_X|_E)$$ induced by the $\rho_i$ is an isomorphism, the filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] being taken in sets, in abelian groups or in commutative rings. The identification is natural for isomorphisms of schemes carrying the indicated opens and intersections to one another.

source.place: Tag 0APJ proof, first paragraph, using equation (equation-sections-of-intersection) from the preceding paragraph

proof.text: Fix an index $i_0$. Each open subscheme $U_i$ is quasi-separated: its affine open cover is also a family of affine opens of $X$, whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion]; clause (2) applied to this cover gives the claim. Since $U_i$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] makes every $U_i$ spectral. In particular $Y=U_{i_0}$ is spectral. Let $J$ be the set of distinct opens among the $U_i$ contained in $Y$, ordered by reverse inclusion, and put $V_j=j$ for $j\in J$. It is a set, is nonempty (it contains $Y$), and is directed by the given refinement condition. Every original $U_i$ contains a member of $J$, by applying that condition to $i,i_0$. Consequently $E=\bigcap_{j\in J}V_j$. For the stipulated finite-intersection refinement, use nonempty finite intersections. Two quasi-compact opens have finite affine covers, so their intersection is covered by finitely many pairwise affine-open intersections, each quasi-compact by clause (1) above. Induction therefore makes every nonempty finite intersection quasi-compact. Their total intersection is unchanged and their family is directed by reverse inclusion.

source.place: Section label section-ind-quasi-affine, equation-sections-of-intersection, reduction to one quasi-compact open; Properties Tag 094L and Schemes Tag 01KO

proof.text: For $j\le k$ let $f_{jk}:V_k\hookrightarrow V_j$ be inclusion. These maps are spectral: a quasi-compact open $W$ of $V_j$ is a quasi-compact open of $Y$ (inclusion preserves its topology and open covers), and $f_{jk}^{-1}(W)=W\cap V_k$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-spectral-space], since $W,V_k$ are quasi-compact opens of $Y$. Identities and composition are those of inclusions. The subspace $E$ is the topological limit of this diagram, with projections $p_j:E\hookrightarrow V_j$. Indeed, the coordinates of a compatible tuple all coincide in $Y$, since any two indices have a common upper bound. That common point lies in every $V_j$, hence in $E$; conversely any point of $E$ gives such a tuple. The initial topology of the $p_j$ is the subspace topology: all inclusions are continuous for that topology, and the projection $p_Y:E\hookrightarrow Y$ alone induces the subspace topology. This also proves the limit assertion when $E$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0A31, label lemma-make-spectral-space, proof of assertion (b): universal property of the limit of the inclusions

proof.text: We may compute the underlying sets of the ring-valued inverse images by the set-valued inverse-image construction, with the same units. To check this, let $h:T\to Z$ be any of the continuous maps used here and let $G$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $Z$. For an open $W\subseteq T$, the opens $B\supseteq h(W)$ form a small nonempty directed poset under reverse inclusion. By [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], the presheaf inverse image is $h_pG(W)=\varinjlim_B G(B)$ in rings. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] its elements are represented by sections on such $B$, and two representatives agree precisely after restriction to a smaller such open. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] these are exactly the representatives and equality relation for the set colimit. Thus the canonical map from the set colimit to the underlying ring colimit is a bijection, commuting with restriction and with the coprojections. Sheafification commutes with underlying sets, including its unit, by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian]. Applying this to $h_pG$ gives the claimed identification of $h^{-1}G$ and its unit on underlying sets.

source.place: Tags 008F and 0087, labels lemma-pullback-presheaves and lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures; Categories Tag 04AX for representatives in filtered colimits

proof.text: For an open inclusion $v:V\hookrightarrow Z$, inverse image is ordinary restriction. In fact every open $W$ of $V$ is open in $Z$, and $W$ is the terminal index of the poset of open neighbourhoods of $v(W)=W$ used in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Thus $v_pG(W)=G(W)$, compatibly with restriction; this presheaf is already a sheaf, so the universal property of sheafification identifies $v^{-1}G$ with $G|_V$. Under this identification the inverse-image unit is the usual restriction map. Let $G$ now denote the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal O_X|_Y$. For $j\in J$, put $v_j:V_j\hookrightarrow Y$ and $H_j=v_j^{-1}G$. The preceding calculation identifies $H_j$ with the underlying structure sheaf on $V_j$. The unit equation for the canonical composition isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition], applied to $E\hookrightarrow Y\hookrightarrow X$, identifies $p_Y^{-1}G$ with the underlying sheaf of $\mathcal O_X|_E$ and identifies its maps from $H_j(V_j)$ with precisely the specified $\rho_j$. Applied to $V_k\hookrightarrow V_j\hookrightarrow Y$, that same equation identifies the transition maps on $H_j(V_j)$ with ordinary restrictions to $V_k$. Step 3 ensures these identifications also describe the underlying maps of the ring-valued units.

source.place: Tags 008F and 008I, labels lemma-pullback-presheaves and lemma-pullback-composition; restriction to an open subspace and compatibility of the composition isomorphism with the units

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-pullback-sections] to the small directed set $J$, the spectral spaces $V_j$, their spectral inclusion maps and the topological limit $E$ from Step 2. Take its fixed index to be $Y\in J$, its sheaf to be $G$, and its quasi-compact open to be all of $Y$. The preimage of this open at stage $j$ is all of $V_j$, and the preimage on the limit is all of $E$. Clause (b) gives: every section of $p_Y^{-1}G$ on $E$ comes from a section of $H_j$ on $V_j$ for some $j\in J$. By Steps 3 and 4 this says exactly $s=\rho_j(a)$ for a structure-sheaf section $a$, proving (a). No ring, scheme structure or nonemptiness of $E$ is required by the cited topological lemma.

source.place: Tag 0A32, label lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit, with fixed index Y and the full quasi-compact open Y; the fixed-sheaf case of Tag 0A33 used in equation-sections-of-intersection

proof.text: For (b), start instead with $i_0=i$ in Steps 1 and 2, so $Y=U_i$ itself is an index in $J$. If $a,a'\in\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X|_{U_i})$ have the same image on $E$, Steps 3 and 4 give sections of $H_Y$ whose images on $E$ agree. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-pullback-sections], at the stage $Y$, gives $k\ge Y$ in $J$ where the two sections agree. By Step 4 this is $a|_{V_k}=a'|_{V_k}$. Choose an original index labelling $V_k$; it satisfies $V_k\subseteq U_i$, as required. Passing to distinct opens in $J$ therefore loses neither representatives nor eventual equalities for the original indexed family.

source.place: Tag 0A32, label lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit, injectivity/eventual equality applied with base open U_i

proof.text: The maps $\rho_i$ are compatible with restriction by Step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], (a) makes the induced set-colimit map surjective. If representatives $a\in\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X)$ and $b\in\Gamma(U_j,\mathcal O_X)$ have the same image on $E$, choose an original stage $h$ contained in $U_i\cap U_j$ and apply (b) to $a|_{U_h},b|_{U_h}$. They agree on a further stage, so the same elementwise lemma proves injectivity. This proves the set-colimit assertion. For abelian groups and rings one can check the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] directly: given a compatible cocone $q_i$ into $B$ in either category, define $q(s)=q_i(a)$ using (a). The eventual equality just proved makes this independent of the choice. To check addition or multiplication, move two representatives to a common stage $h$ and compute $q(s+t)=q_h(a|_{U_h}+b|_{U_h})=q(s)+q(t)$ and, in rings, $q(st)=q_h(a|_{U_h}b|_{U_h})=q(s)q(t)$. Zero, negatives and the unit are checked at one stage. Each $\rho_i$ preserves these operations because it is a ring inverse-image unit. Uniqueness of $q$ follows from (a). Hence this same section ring, or its underlying abelian group, is the specified colimit, with the specified canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 04AX and 002F, labels section-directed-colimits and definition-colimit; elementwise criterion and direct verification of the algebraic universal properties

proof.text: Finally let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X'$ carry the indicated open family and $E$ to the corresponding family and $E'$. Its structure-sheaf isomorphism gives maps $g_i^\sharp:\Gamma(U'_i,\mathcal O_{X'})\to\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X)$ and $g_E^\sharp$ on the inverse-image sheaves over $E',E$. They satisfy $g_E^\sharp\rho'_i=\rho_i g_i^\sharp$: on the presheaf inverse image this equality holds on each representative section over an open neighbourhood, since both composites restrict its pullback by $g$; it then holds on sheafifications by uniqueness in the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Consequently the two maps from the colimit agree after each coprojection, and hence agree by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This proves naturality of exactly the canonical identification, in all three categories. In particular the empty intersection causes no exception: the topological lemma covers it, and the sheaf over the empty space has its unique section (the zero ring in the ring case).
